results.title: GoldBod among 20 companies in SEC’s expanded virtual asset sandbox
results.content: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has increased the number of companies admitted into its virtual asset regulatory sandbox from 11 to 20 as it gathers information to guide the regulation of digital asset services in Ghana. The expansion is intended to give the regulator a broader understanding of the services being offered under the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act, 2025 (Act 1154), and help shape the licensing framework for the sector. Speaking at the Africa Virtual Assets Summit 2026, the Acting Director-General of the SEC, Dr James Klutse Avedzi, said the additional companies would provide the regulator with more data on the different activities taking place in the virtual asset industry. He identified tokenisation as one of the services covered by the regulatory framework, describing it as an established licensing category.

results.title: What Is Wrong With Us: Africa cannot blame its way to economic freedom
results.content: A remarkable talent has quietly flourished across our continent, and it is the ability to explain almost any problem with breathtaking precision. We know who caused it, which administration inherited it, which one worsened it, which international institution contributed to it and which foreign power ought to apologise for it. We can debate yesterday's mistakes for hours, form committees to investigate them, and, when those committees report, form fresh committees to discover why the first recommendations were never implemented. Meanwhile the drain remains blocked, the factory stays shut, the graduate is still unemployed, the farmer still cannot reach the market, and an African child is still waiting for a future promised before her parents were born. results.title: PWREP challenges prosecution to prove GH¢49.1m in Adu-Boahene trial was public money
results.content: The Parties Without Representation in Parliament (PWREP) has challenged the prosecution in the trial of former National Signals Bureau Director-General Kwabena Adu-Boahene to establish that the GH¢49.1 million at the centre of the case was public money. The group argues that the State must prove the ownership and source of the disputed funds rather than rely solely on evidence that money was transferred between bank accounts. According to PWREP, the prosecution must demonstrate whether the funds formed part of an approved government allocation or were released through the government's financial management system. It maintains that establishing the public ownership of the money is central to proving the alleged theft and financial loss to the State.

results.title: GACL to pay first-ever dividend to government since 2007

results.title: PWREP questions State’s case against Adu Boahene, raises concerns over judges’ vehicles
results.content: The Parties Without Representation in Parliament (PWREP) has questioned the strength of the State’s case against former National Signals Bureau Director-General Kwabena Adu Boahene, arguing that evidence presented by prosecution witnesses has failed to establish a case capable of securing his conviction. PWREP says the prosecution’s case remains weak when assessed against the evidence on record and has warned that continuing proceedings without sufficient evidence could undermine the administration of justice. In a statement, the group argued that the burden of proof rests with the State and that an accused person should not be expected to prove his innocence. “The State has failed to adduce sufficient evidence to establish a case capable of securing the conviction of Adu Boahene,” the statement said.
